method: Free public global research, direct official funder and linked application retrieval, timestamp-guarded updates, existing record_funding_status_check audit RPC and production read-back.

records.title: Pollination Project Seed Grants
records.deadline: November 30, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. (funder says US Eastern, official portal says Pacific); reopens January 1, 2027.
records.notes: The funder application page says 11:59 p.m. US Eastern and the linked portal says 11:59 p.m. PST for the annual pause. The published times conflict, so no actionable status or exact cutoff was assigned.

records.title: Pulitzer Center — Rainforest Reporting Grant
records.deadline: We accept grant proposals on a rolling basis.
records.amount: Project-based reporting costs; amount depends on proposal
records.eligibility: Staff and freelance journalists reporting on tropical rainforests in the Amazon, Central Africa or Southeast Asia. Applications may be submitted in English, Spanish, Portuguese, French or Bahasa Indonesia. A project description, budget and distribution plan are required.
records.summary: Reporting grants for underreported issues affecting tropical rainforests, including Central Africa. Submit through the official multilingual application form.
records.notes: The official page was independently readable through public web research and explicitly describes rolling intake. Its linked FormAssembly form is live, but the direct funder-page fetch returned HTTP 403. Current status remains unconfirmed.

records.title: Rare Disease Reporting Fellowship and Grants 2026 (up to $2,000)
records.amount: Up to US$2,000 for up to 20 qualifying fellows
records.eligibility: Working journalists, including freelancers, able to attend the November 16–20 online training and publish a rare disease story by March 1, 2027. Reporting grants are conditional on selection and qualification.
records.summary: Journalism training fellowship with conditional reporting grants. The application deadline has passed.
records.notes: The official National Press Foundation page gives an October 22 deadline and distinguishes fellowship training from conditional reporting grants. The imported listing is corrected to a closed fellowship.

records.title: 2026 CEGA Global Networks Research Grant Competition
records.eligibility: Restricted to teams with at least one CEGA Fellow and one CEGA Affiliate, with eligible research in specified East and West African countries. UC Berkeley PhD students may apply with a CEGA Affiliate sponsoring the study. Research must credibly identify causal effects; purely qualitative or descriptive studies do not qualify.
records.summary: Research funding for policy-relevant impact evaluations in eligible African countries. This call requires CEGA network membership and a joint research team.
records.notes: The official call explicitly invites proposals and the linked Submittable manager lists the matching active cycle and submission link. The funder publishes a date-only cutoff. The portal encodes 2026-11-16 08:00:00Z, retained as additional evidence without inventing a displayed timezone.

records.title: Save Our Seas Ocean Storytelling Photography Grant 2026
records.amount: Fully funded conservation photography assignment, including day rate and travel
records.eligibility: Early-career or emerging conservation photographers worldwide, including African applicants, with no more than five years of experience in a photography-related discipline. Applicants with another current Save Our Seas Foundation grant cannot apply. A portfolio and photo story are required.
records.summary: Two selected photographers receive funded assignments and mentorship to tell ocean conservation stories. Subjects may include marine wildlife, habitats, fisheries and coastal communities.
records.notes: The funder explicitly states this photography call is open and gives an exact CET cutoff. The official linked grants portal is reachable and describes account-based applications.

records.title: Commonwealth Blue Charter Incubator Round II
records.deadline: Funder page: Friday 11 December 2026, 23:59 GMT (UTC+0). Application form: 11th December 2026 Midnight GMT (UTC+0).
records.eligibility: Lead applicants must be legally established national or sub-national government entities from a Commonwealth member country. Eligible African Commonwealth governments may apply. NGO, research and private-sector organisations may participate as confirmed implementation partners. Each country may submit at most two proposals and each government lead at most one.
records.summary: Grants for government-led ocean and sustainable blue economy projects. The official form and call page give different closing-time wording, so applicants need to check the cutoff with the funder.
records.notes: The call explicitly states Round II is live and all 56 Commonwealth member countries are eligible. The linked SurveyMonkey form is active but uses ambiguous midnight wording instead of the page’s 23:59 GMT. No exact instant or actionable open status was assigned.

records.title: Crowder-Messersmith Conservation Fund 2027
records.eligibility: Early-stage conservation and public education projects in developing countries, including eligible African countries. Projects must benefit threatened or endangered species or habitat, involve local communities, and finish within one year. Funds go to an organisation’s bank account. Projects in conflict zones or countries under US banking sanctions are excluded.
records.summary: Seed grants for local nature conservation and public education. Download the application and instructions and email it as an attachment to CMaward@natureforward.org.
records.notes: The official page still explicitly says 2027 applications are open September 1–December 1, 2026. Its current instructions PDF returned HTTP 200. Email the completed form to CMaward@natureforward.org. No closing time or timezone is published.

records.title: MQA Special Projects and Partnerships Discretionary Grants 2026–2027
records.deadline: 23:59 on Friday, 20 November 2026. Later applications may be accepted until 28 February 2027, subject to available funding and programme requirements.
records.amount: Subject to MQA budget, approved proposal and funding rules
records.eligibility: Legally registered public or private entities in South Africa, including companies, public bodies, universities, colleges, research institutions, NGOs, NPOs and community-based organisations. Projects must address mining and minerals sector skills-development priorities and meet the mandatory registration, tax, financial, capacity and application requirements.
records.summary: Discretionary grants for strategic skills-development initiatives in the mining and minerals sector. Download and complete the prescribed form and email the signed application, proposal and supporting documents to SpecialProjects@mqa.org.za.
records.notes: The current official call invites applications and the linked guidelines confirm South African entity eligibility. The application form is reachable. The published primary cutoff specifies 23:59 but no timezone. The later February date is conditional and is not a guaranteed extension.

records.title: Unearthodox Exploration Co-Lab 2027
records.amount: CHF 10,000 grant plus a 10-month incubation programme
records.eligibility: Open internationally, including Africa, to initiatives at the intersection of environmental and societal change. Applicants must be beyond the idea stage with groundwork such as research, testing, a pilot or community engagement. The programme is conducted in English and regular online calls use the UTC−6 to UTC+6 range.
records.summary: An online incubation programme for initiatives addressing root causes in the relationship between people and nature, with CHF 10,000 grant funding and tailored support. The cohort runs March–December 2027.
records.notes: The official funder page explicitly invites applications through November 16 and links the live YouNoodle programme page. That page says Open, supplies an Apply now route and publishes the exact GMT+1 cutoff. Funding is paired with participation in the incubation programme.

records.title: IKI Small Grants 2027, Eighth Call
records.deadline: Eligibility registration closes 8 January 2027. Invited eligible organisations must submit project proposals by 16 March 2027.
records.eligibility: Local organisations in ODA-eligible countries, including eligible African countries, with average annual revenue of €60,000–€500,000 over the last three years. Nonprofits and private organisations pursuing nonprofit objectives are eligible. Individuals, one-person organisations, government bodies and branches of organisations based in non-ODA countries are excluded. Proposals must address eligible climate or biodiversity objectives and meet the full funding rules.
records.summary: Climate and biodiversity grants with capacity development. The eligibility-registration window is announced to open November 15, 2026. Project proposals are invited only after eligibility review.
records.notes: The official page says the eighth call will open November 15. Today is November 12, so this is upcoming. Application guidelines and the active route are scheduled to be published on the opening date. No application URL or precise opening or closing time was invented.

key_evidence.finding: Current window opened October 26. The primary November 20 at 23:59 cutoff has no published timezone. Acceptance after that date through February 28 is conditional.
Legally registered South African public and private entities may apply, subject to sector alignment and compliance. Applications must include the signed form, proposal and supporting documents.

Programme page explicitly says Open, provides an Apply now link, confirms CHF 10,000 grant funding and publishes November 16 at 11:59 PM GMT+1. It accepts international initiatives and describes English-language participation.
Eighth call is announced to open November 15. Eligibility registrations close January 8, with a separate March 16 invited-proposal deadline. No live application route was yet published.
